title: Verifier-integrated LLM intent→configuration pipeline: an artifact-grounded paired evaluation and lessons from a ceiling effect
abstract: We preregistered and executed a deterministic paired experiment (CNSM2026-GVR-AV1-001) that tested whether integrating an automated network verifier (block-on-violation) into an LLM intent→configuration pipeline reduces unsafe enactments. Using gpt-5-mini under a shared-initial generation policy on 150 paired intents (300 episodes), both the baseline (LLM-only) and guarded (LLM+verifier-block) pipelines produced identical candidates that the deterministic validator accepted in every episode (n11=150; n10=n01=n00=0). The preregistered inferential test is therefore uninformative (McNemar two-sided p = 1.0); paired-bootstrap 95% CI for the paired difference = [0.0, 0.0] (10,000 resamples, seed=1729). We release the full artifact bundle (preregistration, execution manifest, per-episode scoring JSONs, response files, and SHA256 hashes), diagnose why a ceiling effect occurred (shared-initial generation + validator acceptance predicates), correct a preregistration–execution mismatch (the preregistered rollback hypothesis was not testable), and provide artifact-grounded recommendations for future verifier evaluation that would expose meaningful discordant outcomes.

sections.introduction: Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly applied to intent-driven NetOps tasks (intent→configuration). To deploy such systems safely, operational architectures commonly pair generation with an automated verifier that either (a) blocks unsafe deployments, (b) triggers repairs, or (c) initiates rollback. We preregistered CNSM2026-GVR-AV1-001 to test whether a block-on-violation verifier reduces unsafe enactments in a paired design (each intent evaluated under baseline and guarded conditions). Our contributions are: (1) a machine-readable preregistration and full execution manifest; (2) a complete, artifact-backed paired run (150 paired tasks) with per-episode validator traces and SHA256 manifests; and (3) an artifact-grounded diagnosis of a deterministic ceiling effect that prevented confirmatory inference, plus concrete, artifact-referenced prescriptions for future evaluations.
sections.related_work: Recent surveys and domain papers argue for verifier- and workflow-centered evaluation of agentic NetOps systems rather than standalone QA metrics (selected verified sources: Augé et al., Aether (W7155247165); Bilal et al., Agentic NetOps survey (W7161354925); Nguyen et al., intent→configuration (doi:10.1002/nem.2313); MeshAgent (W4416927413)). Generate→validate→repair patterns are well-studied in program repair and AIOps literatures and motivate our paired design and preregistration (see referenced verified records). Prior work emphasizes adversarial/stateful tasks, multi-verifier matrices, and independent per-condition generation to reveal verifier value—guidance we adopt in our recommendations after diagnosing the current run's ceiling.
sections.methodology: Preregistration and design. We froze a machine-readable preregistration (CNSM2026-GVR-AV1-001; preregistration SHA256 = 66fbf2c56649115c66412326fcc739ebacced84ec2df3fca796f4e7eac4a9b04) before observing outcomes. Design: paired binary episodes; 150 distinct intents stratified equally across three ambiguity strata (benign / ambiguous / partially-specified) → 50 tasks per stratum; each task executed under two conditions (baseline, guarded) yielding 300 episodes. Model and generation policy. Model: gpt-5-mini (recorded in model_configuration.json; SHA256 = 1acce92558edeb13cd97b75817329d332afe4a36d01d566f1a26c61b132923fa). Generation policy: shared_initial_candidate (one initial generation call per task; independent-condition generation was not used; this is recorded in the execution manifest). Verifier and scoring. Verifier/scorer: deterministic_netops_validator_v5; per-episode deterministic scoring JSONs were recorded at execution/scoring/*.json (representative file execution/scoring/task-000001-guarded.json; SHA256 = 974cab2a4237a0fca9ebe61616d6b471cf2e6bfbd5e5cbabe82701957cbeea14). Primary estimand and analysis. Primary estimand: per-task unsafe-enactment rate difference (LLM-only minus LLM+verifier-block), operationalized as a binary outcome where an episode is unsafe iff the verifier JSON had valid==false or violation_count>0. Analysis: paired McNemar two-sided test (preregistered), with paired-bootstrap percentile 95% CI (10,000 resamples, seed=1729) as an exacting complement. Contamination and exclusion rules. Automatic exclusions were enforced per preregistration: non-RFC1918 addresses or detected organization names in outputs, and exact-match fingerprinting against curated public-repo fingerprints (detection rules and logs archived; contamination summary path analysis/contamination_summary.csv SHA256 = 389227f0d1e81239c7498abd4944a04c59c92c5fa042b990e332796cd61c3222). Execution artifacts and reproducibility. All provider-call traces, responses, scoring JSONs, hashes, and analysis scripts are archived (execution manifest; full SHA256 manifest referenced in the manifest). Representative response file: execution/responses/task-000001-guarded.txt SHA256 = 8f38c8becd7e1e36d8902e9ba2f09218baad021d77365b20eb52914a4bdf4080. Paired contingency table stored at analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv (SHA256 = c2ba9cdb5d0938eae910129ba511eadf309319e6e05b36d9e3b4860032deb80e).
sections.results: Execution summary (artifact-backed). The run completed all planned episodes: planned_episode_count=300, completed_episode_count=300, model_calls_used=150 (one initial generation per task), failed_episode_count=0 (see execution manifest). Scoring outcomes: every generated candidate was accepted by the verifier in both conditions. Aggregated counts (from analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv; SHA256 = c2ba9cdb5d09...): n11=150, n10=0, n01=0, n00=0. Inferential outputs (preregistered): McNemar two-sided exact p = 1.0; paired-bootstrap 95% CI for paired difference = [0.0, 0.0] (10,000 resamples, seed=1729). Interpretation: these statistics are deterministic consequences of the observed contingency (no discordant pairs). They do not demonstrate equivalence or lack of verifier utility; instead they indicate that the experimental design and execution produced identical, validator-acceptable candidates in both conditions (a ceiling effect). Representative episode artifacts. Three representative per-episode artifacts (responses and scoring JSONs) are archived and cited so readers may inspect exact transcripts and validator fields: (1) task-000001 — response execution/responses/task-000001-guarded.txt SHA256 = 8f38c8be..., scoring JSON execution/scoring/task-000001-guarded.json SHA256 = 974cab2a...; (2) task-000002 — response execution/responses/task-000002-guarded.txt SHA256 = ae967f70..., scoring JSON execution/scoring/task-000002-guarded.json SHA256 = da5d1257...; (3) task-000003 — response execution/responses/task-000003-guarded.txt SHA256 = f7f4db24..., scoring JSON execution/scoring/task-000003-guarded.json SHA256 = 5767abe5.... Validator fields recorded per episode include valid (boolean), violation_count (integer), difficulty.pattern (string), required_command_count and parsed_command_count; these fields underlie our diagnosis and recommendations and are visible inside the archived JSONs.
sections.discussion: Artifact-grounded diagnosis of the ceiling effect. Two deterministic, archived facts explain why the preregistered hypothesis test was uninformative: (A) shared-initial generation: by design the pipeline used a shared_initial_candidate policy (one initial generation call per task shared across conditions) and the recorded per-response SHA256s are identical across baseline and guarded files for every task (e.g., execution/responses/task-000001-baseline.txt SHA256 = 8f38c8be... equals execution/responses/task-000001-guarded.txt SHA256 = 8f38c8be...); (B) verifier acceptance: deterministic_netops_validator_v5 marked every candidate as valid (violation_count==0, valid==true) across all episodes (see execution/scoring/*.json; representative SHA256s cited above). Consequence: the guarded pipeline had no divergent candidates to block, so no discordant pairs existed. Preregistration–execution mismatch. The preregistered secondary hypothesis (H2: rollback effectiveness) required verifier-detected violations and invocation of rollback; because no violations occurred the rollback branch was never executed and H2 was not testable in this run (artifact-backed; no rollback traces in scoring JSONs or execution manifest). Threats to validity and construct limits. Construct validity: the verifier used here enforces syntactic and per-command predicate checks recorded in each scoring JSON (fields such as required_command_count, parsed_command_count), but—per the archived difficulty.pattern values—did not exercise richer temporal/ reachability invariants or emulated canary tests that would have detected certain classes of unsafe transient behavior (these limitations are visible in the validator fields within the archived JSONs). External validity: single model (gpt-5-mini) and single verifier limit generalization. Operational implication: verifier value cannot be demonstrated unless generation and benchmark tasks are co-designed to produce verifier-sensitive, potentially unsafe candidates under baseline generation. Artifact-grounded prescriptions. Based on the recorded artifacts we recommend future confirmatory evaluations (all prescriptions are implementable using the archived run's scripts and traces): (1) independent per-condition generation (remove shared_initial_candidate) so baseline and guarded pipelines may propose different candidates; (2) adversarial & stateful task bank that encodes temporal invariants (use recorded difficulty.pattern values such as "make_before_break_uplink_switchover", "paired_link_atomic_mtu_change", "shutdown_configure_restore" as templates to synthesize tasks that exercise transient/ordering constraints); (3) multi-verifier evaluation matrices (add reachability/SMT/header-space verifiers to detect violations that syntactic predicates miss); (4) instrumented canary reachability tests in the emulation and record canary failure traces so rollback hypotheses are testable; (5) multi-model experiments to measure model-specific fragility. All required artifacts and SHA256 pointers to the example difficulty.pattern strings and scoring JSONs are provided for reproducibility.
sections.conclusion: We preregistered and executed a paired experiment comparing LLM-only and LLM+verifier-block pipelines for intent→configuration translation. The execution produced identical, verifier-accepted candidates in all 150 paired tasks, yielding a deterministic ceiling (n11=150) that made the preregistered confirmatory comparisons uninformative. The paper's scientific value is artifact-backed: (i) a complete, reproducible execution bundle (preregistration, provider-call traces, per-episode scoring JSONs, response transcripts, analysis scripts, and full SHA256 manifest); (ii) a clear diagnosis of why the run produced a ceiling effect; and (iii) concrete, artifact-grounded recommendations for verifier evaluation designs that would produce informative discordant outcomes. We release all traces and hashes so other researchers can replay, adversarialize, and extend the pipeline to measure verifier utility under conditions that exercise transient and reachability invariants.

The exact initial master prompt and autonomy constraints used to start the autonomous run are archived verbatim within the frozen preregistration artifact referenced above (see preregistration SHA256). Orchestration/framework: the execution adapter family is hosted_netops_gvr_v1 (recorded in the execution manifest). Generation policy and call budget: the preregistered generation policy was shared_initial_candidate (one initial model call per task; at most one repair call permitted), and the run used 150 model calls (one per task) as recorded in the execution manifest. Verifier and scoring: deterministic_netops_validator_v5 served as the automated verifier/scorer; per-episode validator traces and scoring JSONs are archived at execution/scoring/*.json (representative file execution/scoring/task-000001-guarded.json SHA256 = 974cab2a4237a0fca9ebe6...). Preregistration/freeze procedure: the preregistration document was frozen before experiment execution (SHA256 above) and includes the full experimental plan (estimands, power plan, exclusion rules, retry policy, contamination plan). Autonomous literature and reference verification: cited literature and related records used in positioning were autonomously discovered and verified; verified items appear in the manuscript's cited_record_ids. Missingness, retries, and restarts: the preregistered retry policy allowed up to three retries for transient provider/infrastructure failures; the run completed with zero failed episodes and followed only the preregistered automated retry policy (no manual reruns to improve outcomes). Deviation disclosure: the preregistered secondary hypothesis (rollback effectiveness) required verifier-detected violations and was not testable in this execution because no verifier-detected violations occurred; this deviation is fully recorded in the archived scoring JSONs and execution manifest. limitations: Ceiling effect: both pipelines produced validator-acceptable configurations in all 150 confirmatory tasks, preventing the preregistered confirmatory hypothesis from producing informative discordant pairs.
Synthetic/emulated benchmark: CNSM-AI-NetOps-Intent-Bench-v1 is synthetic/emulated and may not exercise live timing/transient invariants present in production NetOps.
Single-model and single-validator scope: experiments used only gpt-5-mini and deterministic_netops_validator_v5; results do not generalize across LLM or verifier families.

Validator construct limits: the validator enforces syntactic and per-command predicates (violation_count, required_command_count, etc.) visible in scoring JSONs, but did not exercise richer reachability/temporal invariants in this run.
Rollback hypothesis untested: the preregistered H2 (automated rollback performance) could not be evaluated because the rollback branch was never invoked; this is disclosed and artifact-backed.
Contamination detection limits: automatic detectors flagged zero contaminated tasks, but heuristic scans cannot eliminate subtle training-data leakage not captured by exact-match detectors.
